title: Merge k Sorted Lists
corePattern: K-Way Merge via Min-Heap and Divide and Conquer
interviewTips: Clarify constraints: what are k (number of lists) vs N (total nodes)? Are lists possibly empty or null? Should you reuse existing nodes or create new ones?

Trade-off: Brute-force sort is O(N log N) and simple but ignores sortedness; Heap is O(N log k) with O(k) extra space and streams results; Divide-and-Conquer is O(N log k) with O(1) heap space but O(log k) recursion stack and reuses pointers.

Edge-case tip: handle lists = [] vs [null], single list, lists with one element, duplicate values (heap comparator must not compare ListNode objects directly), and avoid cycles by advancing pointers correctly.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Collect All Values and Sort
approaches.intuition: Ignore that each list is sorted, dump every value into an array, sort it, then rebuild a new sorted linked list.
approaches.theory: If there are N total nodes, collecting is O(N). Sorting dominates at O(N log N). Rebuilding is O(N). This is correct because sorted array order equals merged sorted list order. It uses O(N) extra space for values plus O(N) for new nodes and does not exploit k-way sorted structure.

timeComplexity.explanation: N is total nodes. Collect O(N) + sort O(N log N) + rebuild O(N).

spaceComplexity.explanation: O(N) for values array plus O(N) for new output nodes (or O(N) if counting output).

steps: Rebuild linked list node by node from sorted array

edgeCases: k=1 single sorted list returns copy of that list

approaches.name: Approach 2: Min-Heap K-Way Merge
approaches.intuition: The merged head is always the minimum among current heads of k lists. Maintain those k candidates in a min-heap, repeatedly pop min and push its next.
approaches.theory: This is classic k-way merge / tournament sort. Heap size <= k. Each of N nodes is pushed and popped once at O(log k) cost, so O(N log k). We splice original nodes (no new allocations except dummy) giving O(k) auxiliary space. Tie-break by list index to avoid comparing nodes when values equal.

timeComplexity.explanation: Each of N nodes pushed/popped once from heap of size at most k, each heap op O(log k).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Heap holds at most one node per list. Output reuses input nodes, O(1) extra besides heap.

edgeCases: All lists empty -> heap empty -> return null
Duplicate values across lists require stable comparator
Large k with many empty lists: only non-null heads pushed

approaches.name: Approach 3: Divide and Conquer Pairwise Merge
approaches.intuition: Merge lists two at a time like merge sort: repeatedly merge pairs with increasing interval until one list remains.
approaches.theory: Merging two sorted lists of total length m is O(m). There are log k levels, each level processes all N nodes once, so O(N log k). Iterative interval doubling avoids recursion depth and achieves O(1) extra space besides output (recursion version uses O(log k) stack). Reuses nodes via standard two-list merge.

timeComplexity.explanation: log k merge rounds, each round merges all N nodes once via linear two-list merges.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Iterative version uses O(1) extra besides output (recursive version O(log k) stack). Nodes reused.

edgeCases: lists = [] returns null without accessing lists[0]
Odd k leaves last list unpaired in a round
k=10000 with empty lists still O(k log k) loop overhead but no node work
